items.title: Trump loses control of Congress
items.text: Following a decisive defeat in the US midterm elections, Donald Trump and the Republican Party have lost control of both houses of Congress to the Democrats. The results have sparked intense disputes within both major parties. Among Republicans, Vice President JD Vance has attributed the electoral losses to the unpopular war with Iran, which created a visible rift with the president. At the same time, Donald Trump has sent mixed signals regarding his policy direction: while publicly acknowledging that his strict immigration enforcement went too far, he appointed Stephen Miller, the architect of those policies, as White House Chief of Staff. On the Democratic side, progressives and moderates are competing to shape the party’s future legislative agenda. Political analysts warn that despite the significant shift in congressional control, deep ideological divisions and the president’s veto power will likely lead to continued political gridlock in Washington rather than major policy changes. Difficult words: dispute (a disagreement, argument, or debate between people, parties, or groups), rift (a serious break in friendly relations between people or groups), gridlock (a situation where no progress can be made because of strong disagreement or opposing forces). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Trump loses control of Congress
items.text: The Democratic Party won big in the US midterm elections and took control of both houses of Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republican Party. This defeat caused strong arguments inside both parties. Vice President JD Vance blamed the election loss on the war with Iran, and disagreed directly with Trump. At the same time, Trump said his strict immigration rules went too far, but he still chose the creator of those rules to lead his White House team. Meanwhile, Democrats are fighting over their plans, as its members want different things. Experts say that even with new Democratic leaders in Congress, it will be hard to pass major new laws because the president can still block them, which may lead to more political delays in Washington. Difficult words: defeat (the loss of a contest, game, election, or battle), blame (to say or think that someone or something is responsible for something bad that happened), major (important, big, serious). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Trump loses control of Congress
items.text: The Democrats win a big election in the US. They now control Congress. President Donald Trump and his team lose many votes . Now, people in both political parties are fighting about what to do next. Vice President JD Vance says that the war with Iran is a bad idea. Many people do not like Trump anymore because of that. Trump said that his immigration rules are too hard. But he still puts his immigration leader in a top job. At the same time, Democrats are trying to agree on new plans for the country. Experts think that it will still be very hard for leaders in Washington to pass new laws and help people quickly. Difficult words: vote (when a person formally chooses a person in an election), immigration rules (what people who come from other countries must and must not do), pass (to officially say yes to a new rule). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Pope Leo visits South America
items.text: Pope Leo drew a crowd of one million people at a nighttime vigil in Buenos Aires on Tuesday during his 12-day South American tour. The pontiff addressed the gathered youth, urged them not to be consumed by the pursuit of wealth, physical appearance, or social media popularity, and warned against humiliating others online. This event followed an outdoor Mass in Cordoba earlier that day, which attracted 650,000 attendees, and a record-breaking gathering of 2.5 million people in Buenos Aires on Monday. As the first pope to visit Catholic-majority Argentina since 1987, Leo seeks to revitalize the Church’s presence in the region against growing evangelical competition. Throughout his visit, the US-born pope has also voiced strong criticism of Argentine President Javier Milei’s strict austerity policies. He argued that government spending cuts disproportionately harm the country’s poorest citizens. Difficult words: pontiff (the Pope, who acts as the chief bishop and leader of the Roman Catholic Church), pursuit (chasing or striving to achieve something), austerity (severity in government spending cutbacks and financial discipline). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Pope Leo visits South America
items.text: Pope Leo spoke to a crowd of one million people during a night event in Buenos Aires, Argentina. He told young people not to focus only on money, physical appearance , or getting likes on social media. This gathering was part of his 12-day trip through South America, which also includes visits to Uruguay and Peru. Large crowds came to see the pope, including 2.5 million people at a historic Mass earlier in the week. Pope Leo is visiting Argentina to support Catholic followers and help poor communities. During his trip, he also asked Argentina’s president not to hurt poor people with government spending cuts . Many residents and students thanked the pope for caring about people in need. Difficult words: physical appearance (the external, visible features of a person), gathering (when many people meet together for a specific event), cut (reduction made to financial spending, resources, or services). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Pope Leo visits South America
items.text: One million people come to see Pope Leo at night in Argentina. The Pope talks to many young people. He asks them to be kind. He tells them not to worry only about money, online popularity , or good looks. Many happy people wave their phones and bring their babies for a blessing . The pope is visiting three countries in South America to talk about God and help poor people. He also asks the country’s leader to help people who do not have much money. Many young people are very happy to see the pope and listen to his words. Difficult words: popularity (when many people like someone), wave (to move your hand when you are saying hello to someone), blessing (a time when people ask for God’s help). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack on freezers
items.text: The French government has blamed Iran for a cyberattack on supermarket freezers and refrigerators across France. The attacks happened last month. They hit around 700 supermarkets and shops. Hackers took control of the cooling systems in the fridges and freezers. Temperatures increased to more than 50 degrees Celsius. Thousands of tons of frozen food melted. Stores had to throw the food away because it was no longer safe to eat. The French Foreign Minister said the attack was on a level never seen before. France believes an Iranian cyber unit carried out the attack. Iran has strongly denied it was involved in the attacks and blamed the French government for them. Security experts have warned that cyberattacks could be more dangerous in the future. Similar attacks have already affected other European countries. A French blood bank has also been hit. Fortunately, workers stopped the blood products from being damaged. Cybersecurity expert Gerome Billois stated: "At the moment, they are attacking easy equipment, but we should be prepared to see attacks on other systems like water or electricity." Weak computer security can let hackers attack places and services, such as hospitals, airports, public transport and banks. This can put people's lives in danger. items.title: Chef fired for refusing to put pineapple on pizza
items.text: An Italian chef in Brisbane, Australia, has been fired for refusing to put pineapple on pizzas, among other reasons. He went to the Fair Work Commission to fight his dismissal, but failed to get his job back. The chef stated that topping pizzas with the tropical fruit was an "insult to his culture". He claimed he was sacked from a restaurant in May after repeatedly refusing his boss's instructions to make pineapple and ham pizzas for diners. His employer contended that the refusal was one of several workplace issues. The commission rejected the chef's application because it was submitted after the deadline. The chef has since found a job at another Italian restaurant. The question of whether pineapple belongs on pizza is a controversial one. It continues to divide public opinion. Pizza purists are aghast at the idea, but it is an established menu staple in many countries. The Hawaiian pizza was reportedly invented in Canada in 1962 after a chef used ham and pineapple as toppings. The restaurant owner expressed his opinion on it. He admitted that while the pizza was not his "absolute favourite," he would not "turn his nose up at it". Many restaurateurs insist that customers should be free to enjoy whatever ingredients and toppings they choose. items.title: Man completes 28-year walk around the world
items.text: A British man has completed an amazing 28-year walk around the world. Former soldier Karl Bushby, 57, arrived home in the city of Hull in England on Monday. He started his adventure in November 1998 in Chile, South America. His plan was to walk all the way home without using cars, boats, buses, trains, or airplanes. During his journey, he travelled about 58,000 kilometres through 29 countries. He crossed frozen seas, deserts, mountains, and jungles. He also faced many dangers. These included encountering polar bears and kidnappers, and spending time in a Russian prison. His journey was expected to take 12 years. However, problems with money, visas, and borders made his trip a lot longer. Thousands of people welcomed Mr Bushby home. He was very happy to finally finish his journey. His mother was waiting outside his childhood home to greet him. Bushby joked: "Sorry to keep you waiting." He also told the cheering crowd that many people around the world had helped him get home. He said he could not have done it alone. Britain's Prime Minister congratulated him on his achievement. He praised Bushby's determination and belief in himself. Bushby told the Guardian newspaper that he wasn't so interested in walking. He said: "It's boring as hell." That didn't stop him walking across four continents. items.title: Study finds majority of pilots nod off mid-flight
items.text: A new report has raised serious concerns about pilot fatigue. The European Cockpit Association (ECA) conducted a survey of nearly 7,200 pilots across 32 countries. It discovered that exhaustion in the cockpit is a widespread and underreported problem. More than three-quarters of respondents said they had briefly dozed off while operating an aircraft in the month before the survey. Almost a quarter of them admitted they continued flying even when they were too tired. Furthermore, half said they had operated a flight when they should have declared themselves unfit for duty. Tiredness can result from long working hours, insufficient rest, and unpredictable schedules. The pilots were very frank in their answers to the survey questions. Many said they were reluctant to report fatigue because they feared punishment or other negative reactions from their bosses. Captain Coen George, a director of the ECA, warned: "When pilots fear career consequences, fatigue goes unreported and the risk returns to the cockpit." Aviation safety experts say exhaustion can impair judgement, slow reaction times and prevent pilots from responding effectively to unexpected in-flight situations. The experts urged airlines to foster a culture in which pilots can report tiredness without fear of repercussions. Carriers should ensure that passenger safety is their top priority. items.title: Love for pumpkin spice
items.text: The average pumpkin spice blend has cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves, and allspice, and for many consumers, it gives the warm, fuzzy feelings. For centuries, people have associated the pumpkin spice flavor with fall. Early American settlers used the same ingredients to preserve the fall harvests of meat, fruit, and vegetables. In 1976, Amelia Simmons wrote a recipe for the flavor in the first American cookbook. In 1934, McCormick made the flavor official with the name pumpkin pie spice. The company gave an easy method to get all the spices needed for pumpkin pie in one shake. In the early 1990s, Starbucks capitalized on the flavor, and the company added the pumpkin spice latte to its repertoire of seasonal drinks. Since then, Starbucks has sold more than 420 million cups in the US alone. People love pumpkin spice as its smell evokes memories. Some experts say the words pumpkin spice can spark cozy fall feelings which people crave at the end of a hot summer. Difficult words: blend (a mixture of different substances), capitalize on (to make profit from something), repertoire (all the items on stock). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Love for pumpkin spice
items.text: Many people love pumpkin spice because it gives them warm cozy feelings. They love to drink to welcome the fall when the hot summer ends. Pumpkin spice has many spices, including cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger, and its smell is very popular. In the 1990s, Starbucks created with the first pumpkin spice latte, and millions of people loved it. Since that time, Starbucks sold more than 420 million cups of pumpkin spice latte in the US, and the company offers it to customers in the fall and winter. The history of pumpkin spice is much older than the 1990s. Hundreds of years ago, American settlers used the same spices to preserve meat, fruit, and vegetables for the winter months. In 1976, author Amelia Simmons wrote a pumpkin spice recipe which she put in the first American cookbook. Difficult words: cozy (something that makes you feel warm and relaxed), settler (a person who moves to survive and live in a new country or area), preserve (to keep food fresh). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Love for pumpkin spice
items.text: People love pumpkin spice. The spice is a mixture of several spices. For example, they are cinnamon, nutmeg , or ginger. It smells very good. It brings happy feelings. No pumpkin is in the mixture. Some people think that Starbucks makes pumpkin spice. The recipe is much older. American settlers use the spices to keep food fresh during the winter. The foods are meat, fruit, and vegetables. In 1976, Amelia Simmons writes a pumpkin spice recipe. She puts pumpkin spice in the first American cookbook. In the 1990s, Starbucks creates the pumpkin spice latte. Many people love it. The drink helps them welcome the fall after a hot summer. Difficult words: mixture (several things put together), nutmeg (a hard seed of a tropical tree), settler (a person who lives in a new country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: 5 Canadian Universities for Indian Students Who Prefer a Smaller City
items.text: Image Source: Magnific A student moving from India to a smaller Canadian city may look forward to finding a few favourite places around campus. As the city will be home during term, a campus tour can help them picture where they would spend their time between classes. They can look for nearby outdoor space or ask about a college community and regular activities they could join. 1. Queen’s University At Queen’s University in Kingston, Campus Life provides information on student clubs, intramurals, recreational activities and volunteering in the city. Students can find activities on campus and ways to meet local people beyond it. The university has broad undergraduate and graduate choices. Applicants still need to choose the level and degree they want and meet its admission requirements. Queen’s offers incoming international first-year undergraduates early move-in access and dedicated academic and career advising. A recurring activity can give students somewhere to return after orientation. Student Academic Success Services provides writing and learning-strategy support. Students can discuss unfamiliar academic expectations there as assignments begin to require more independent work. Students considering residence should check the conditions in their offer. Residence has Living Learning Communities and interest-based options, but a bed-space commitment does not promise a particular room or building. Those conditions belong alongside the decision to study in Kingston. 2. The University of Guelph The campus is in Guelph in southwestern Ontario, with organized activities and nearby outdoor space students can use during the week. The Arboretum connects to campus through trails and forest. Outdoor space is another part of the setting to consider alongside the city’s size. At the University of Guelph , GryphLife brings together clubs, events, workshops and co-curricular opportunities. Student Volunteer Connections helps students find community volunteering that suits their interests and availability. A regular activity offers contact with people beyond orientation. International applicants from India can contact an in-country representative with admissions questions. Global Pre-Arrival Support advisors help new students with registration, housing and arrival matters. GO Transit serves the campus and provides a connection with the Toronto region. Students considering visits or commuting can check the current timetable from the intended starting point. 3. items.title: Sharks in an aquarium
items.text: Visitors at a South Korean aquarium watched in amazement at a shark swimming in a tank with another shark’s tail hanging out of its mouth. While sharks do not tend to eat others of the same species when they are in captivity and they have regular feeds, experts at the aquarium said that sharks have their own territory, and when they occasionally bump against each other, they bite out of astonishment . The smaller shark which fell prey to its bigger counterpart was a banded hound shark. The bigger beast was a sand tiger shark. Difficult words: tend (to do something regularly), species (a kind of animal), astonishment (great surprise), counterpart (a similar animal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Sharks in an aquarium
items.text: At a South Korean aquarium, a shark swam into an even bigger shark, and the bigger shark ate it! For some time, the big shark swam around, and the tail of its prey hung out of its mouth. The visitors of the aquarium looked on in amazement . Sharks do not usually eat each other in captivity , but they have to have their own territory. Difficult words: prey (an animal another animal eats), amazement (surprise, shock), captivity (not free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
